prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” interior painting company for everyone in St. Louis — the right choice depends on your priorities (budget, speed, level of finish, eco‑friendly products, etc.). I can’t browse current reviews from here, but I can help you find the best contractor for your needs. Quick approach and next steps:

What to look for
- License & insurance: contractor should carry general liability and worker’s comp.
- Written estimate: detailed scope (prep, number of coats, trim, ceilings), materials, time frame, payment schedule.
- Portfolio & references: pictures of finished jobs and recent customer references.
- Prep & repairs: how they handle patching, sanding, caulking, priming — prep quality matters most.
- Paint brands & VOCs: which paint they use (e.g., Benjamin Moore, Sherwin‑Williams), and low‑VOC options if desired.
- Warranty/guarantee: how they handle touchups and issues after completion.
- Cleanup & protection: how they protect floors, furniture, and HVAC vents.
- Communication & timeline: clear start/end dates and who your point of contact is.

Where to find/research companies
- Google & Google Maps (customer reviews)
- Yelp and Angi (formerly Angie’s List)
- Better Business Bureau (complaints/history)
- Houzz and Nextdoor for local recommendations
- Ask neighbors or local Facebook community groups

Typical price ranges (ballpark)
- Per square foot: roughly $1.50–$4.00 per sq. ft. (varies by prep and paint quality)
- Per room: commonly $300–$1,000 depending on size, ceiling height, and prep needs
- Whole house: several thousand dollars — get multiple bids for accuracy

Questions to ask when getting an estimate
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide certificates?
- Can you provide written references or photos of similar jobs?
- What brand and sheen of paint will you use? How many coats?
- How do you handle surface repairs and priming?
- What is included in the price? (trim, doors, closets, cleanup)
- What is the timeline and payment schedule? Any deposit required?
- Do you offer a warranty or touch-up guarantee?

If you want, tell me:
- Your neighborhood or ZIP code
- Size of the job (number of rooms, square footage)
- Any special needs (high ceilings, wallpaper removal, woodwork staining, low‑VOC paint)

I can then give more targeted advice and help you evaluate 3–5 contractors you find, or suggest search phrases and review metrics to narrow choices.
